accuracy.evidence: Follows the England National Curriculum Year 1 handwriting requirements (form capital letters, begin and finish in the right place) and common school letter-formation schemes: in print, every capital touches the top line and sits on the base line with no descender, straight strokes start at the top, crossbars go left to right, C and O start near the top and go anticlockwise, and D's curve goes clockwise from the top of the stem.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the errors teachers report in 5 to 6 year olds: starting strokes at the bottom (tag bottom), making capitals x-height (short), letting P or G hang like p and g (hang, the step 1 prediction), floating letters above the line (float), reversed letters (the Made well? step's back option), drawing C and O clockwise (clock) and crossing right to left (rtl).

lab_distinct.evidence: flag_caps.js is about forming capitals on handwriting lines: tapping the capital in five mixed pairs, tracing L, E, A and X from a green start dot along each stroke in order, tracing C, O and D in the right direction, and judging which of three H, N, B and S shapes is made well. It is not the existing phonics or letter-sound labs with new labels, and it passed the 30% shingle gate.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child discovers the rules by doing them: in the pairs the capitals light up as the tall ones on the line; tracing will not start unless the pencil is on the start dot and gives a message when they start at the wrong end; the curve step shows C and O going over the top to the left; and the made-well step makes them check height, line and direction together.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with real wrong pulls: 'Small p hangs below the line. Does capital P hang down too?' (many children copy the small p), 'Where does your pencil start for the long line in L?' (bottom is common) and 'Which way does O go round?'. Each is then tested on the lines and the reveal names what they predicted.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions, e.g. 'Does capital G hang below the line like small g?' and 'Which way do you draw the line across the middle of A?'. Each wrong option has its own message, e.g. 'The dashed line is for small letters like e. Capitals go up to the top line.' and 'C and O go over the top to the left. Only D goes round to the right.'

readability.evidence: Family audience for ages 5 to 6: kid paragraphs use very short sentences and the words top line, base line, start, down, across, and pass the FK 5.0 target; adult paragraphs pass 10.0 and explain the rules, named mistakes and how to use the lab. Instructions on the canvas are one short line each.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate passed. Every kid sentence is a rule or an example letter. Hints name the exact check (start at the top, sit on the line), not general encouragement, and there is no repeated template text across steps.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 (390 px) screenshots on every step before and after Show me: after fixing an overflow bug (text baseline changing the measured cap height), every glyph fits inside its box with the writing lines visible, letter buttons are big tap targets for young children, and the tracing area and direction buttons fit without clipping.

accessibility.evidence: All tracing has button twins (pick the right start and direction, e.g. 'From the top right, over the top and round to the left'), capitals can be chosen with letter buttons, and the made-well step uses numbered buttons. The aria-label updates with each message, feedback is in words, and walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA found no violations in light and dark on desktop and iPhone 13.
